title: Computing diversity metrics for the dataset dashboard
prompt: A dashboard reports diversity metrics (class balance, demographic coverage, duplication rate) over very large training datasets. How should the metrics be computed to back the dashboard?
constraint: Metrics span huge datasets but are viewed only occasionally; freshness-to-the-minute is not required, and cost matters.

options.why: Amortizes one expensive full scan per day and serves instant reads — daily freshness easily satisfies a dashboard that doesn't need minute-level accuracy, and cost stays bounded and predictable. Directly matches the constraint.

Defensible — it spends nothing while nobody looks, which suits occasional viewing. But each cold view triggers a full scan of a huge dataset, making the first load slow and its cost spiky; only viable with caching to dodge repeat scans, so it's weaker than scheduled precompute.
Pays for always-on stream infrastructure to keep metrics minute-fresh — exactly the freshness the constraint says is not needed, while violating the cost concern for a rarely-viewed dashboard.
Recomputing aggregates on each write to a huge dataset burns continuous compute to maintain freshness nobody requires — the worst fit for 'viewed occasionally, cost matters.'
